subject: geography
title: India’s ends, its clock and its neighbours

nodes: Northernmost: the Siachen Glacier region (37° 6′ N)
props.label: North to south, p.54

scenes.narration: The northernmost point of India is in the Siachen Glacier region of the Karakoram range. The southernmost point of the mainland is Kanniyakumari. They are 3,214 kilometres apart.

nodes: Westernmost: the Rann of Kutchch, Gujarat (68° 7′ E)
Almost 30° apart: a two-hour time lag
India follows the time at 82° 30′ E: IST
props.label: Indian Standard Time, p.54

scenes.narration: From Arunachal Pradesh in the east to Gujarat in the west, India is almost 30 degrees wide, so there is a two-hour time lag. To avoid confusion, India follows the time at 82 degrees 30 minutes east: Indian Standard Time.

nodes: South, across the sea: Sri Lanka, the Maldives
props.label: Neighbours, p.54

scenes.narration: Seven countries share land boundaries with India. Across the sea to the south are the islands of Sri Lanka and the Maldives. The Palk Strait and the Gulf of Mannar separate India from Sri Lanka.

questions.prompt: Why does India follow one standard time?
options: To avoid confusion from the two-hour time lag
